rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and visible ICM, but the image does not clearly support a confidently 'top-tier' TE assessment; some described details (minor vacuole/refractile body, uniform cohesive TE) are somewhat speculative from this single image.

Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, repeated failed cycles, prior biochemical losses/miscarriage, sperm motility, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality to frame prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, especially the contrast between good embryo morphology and recurrent failure suggesting non-embryonic factors; however, some causal inferences are stronger than the evidence supports.

Core points on morphology, age-related prognosis, and considering uterine evaluation/endometriosis management are aligned, but several recommendations (ERA as 'critical,' NK testing/intralipids/IVIG, empiric steroids/aspirin, broad thrombophilia work-up, routine PGT-A at age 27) are not strongly guideline-supported.
Provides clear next-step suggestions for transfer support and future work-up, but some recommendations are overly aggressive or insufficiently evidence-based for routine use in this scenario.
